recheck.text: Whether the documentation and release records describe the change: docs/api.md (endpoint, ticket field, filter, audit action, notification), README command-line columns, a CHANGELOG.md section with a version bump in package.json, and a decision record if a format or rule changed.

defects.title: An assignee name with invalid UTF-8 is accepted and stored with a replacement character
defects.repro: Start the service; POST /tickets {"title":"a","requester":"r"}; send PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee with Content-Type application/json and the raw bytes {"assignee":"da\xFFna"} (e.g. printf '{"assignee":"da\377na"}' | curl -X PUT --data-binary @- -H 'Content-Type: application/json' localhost:$PORT/tickets/T-0001/assignee); GET /tickets/T-0001
defects.observed: 200; assignee "da�na" stored, a ticket.assigned audit entry and a notification to "da�na"
defects.expected: 400 invalid with the ticket, audit and outbox unchanged (the byte is not text; the name the client sent is not the one stored)

defects.title: A repeated status or priority filter now lists nothing where 1.4.0 used the first value
defects.expected: The 1.4.0 answer, [T-0001] (the first value), or a 400 refusal; the change is documented in CHANGELOG 1.5.0 as a fix but alters an existing query that returned tickets

defects.title: A malformed UTF-8 byte in the assignee filter matches the agent whose name holds U+FFFD
defects.repro: Start the service. POST /tickets {"title":"A","requester":"r@example.com"}; PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee {"assignee":"Da\uFFFDna"} (200); GET /tickets?assignee=Da%FFna
defects.expected: 400 invalid or an empty page, as the PUT refuses malformed UTF-8 (the product's own spec clause C-52 requires this)
